output.reason: Two days of black tarry stools with lightheadedness on standing suggests ongoing upper GI bleeding with possible significant blood loss, requiring immediate emergency assessment, labs, and endoscopy capability.
output.patientMessage: Go to the emergency department now. Black, tarry stools for two days with lightheadedness when you stand can mean active bleeding in your digestive tract and meaningful blood loss. Do not drive yourself — have someone take you, or call 911 if you feel faint, collapse, vomit blood, or develop chest pain or shortness of breath on the way.
differential: Upper GI bleed (e.g. peptic ulcer, gastritis, varices) causing melena
Other source of melena, including small bowel or right colonic bleeding
